rows.text:
Flyers for the Upside-Down Restaurant are scattered here and there, though some of their claims rather unbelievable...

"Upside-Down" represents a
free-spirited, uninhibited, and utterly laid-back way of life
Ever wondered what your favorite superstar idol is eating?
Today, the secret recipes of the stars are revealed at last
...

Cosmic Film Star: Holy Wubbaboo
"Premium Hand-Poured Oriental Beauty Tea" & "Tingling Truffle Chocolate"

When the bite of tingling peppercorns and the rich sweetness of chocolate simultaneously detonate across the palate, take a sip of hot tea. Ride the wave of scalding water and agony, with your lips the color of grilled sausage, and all five senses activated. It's the surest way to enlightenment.

Holy Wubbaboo's sincere recommendation: "This treat packs a mean punch!"

During the filming of Holy Wubbaboo Adventure 18: Wubbaboo Wars, Holy Wubbaboo reportedly consumed this snack every morning for 37 consecutive days. This ritual is said to have limbered up his joints, as well as kept his spirits fired up, his figure plump and rosy, and his mental state strong.

Viral Influencer: Mr. Ratite
"Raw Terror Shrimp Pickles" & "Scalegorge Vinegar Fish Stirred Noodles"

Two particularly challenging recipes. As the centerpiece of the "Authentic Flavor" series, the chef goes to great lengths during preparation to keep the natural essence of the fish and shrimp intact. The seasoning choice of soy-braised rice vinegar from the last Amber Era allows the shrimp to taste like shrimp, and the fish to taste like fish.

Mr. Ratite's raving recommendation: "Excellent. The shrimp is still breathing, and the fish died for nothing... This restaurant never stops taunting me!"

These were the words of wisdom shared by Mr. Ratite after receiving his dish and engaging in a 50 minute free-for-all brawl with live pickled shrimp, and sampling the "Scalegorge Vinegar Fish Stirred Noodles." This establishment believes that this unique experience was the core source of inspiration behind Mr. Ratite's show "365 Days Living With 108 True Stings."

King of Work: Chrissas the Great
"Mung Bean Sukiyaki" & "Sugar Glazed Donuts"

The bearing of an aristocrat meets the mundane reality of everyday life. This meal combo is the perfect marriage of both worlds. Unbeatable value. Don't miss out.

Chrissas the Great's imperial recommendation: "Come and dine, ye commoners... Do I get to eat for free if I say this to the camera?"

Chrissas the Great, who had gone a long stretch without a proper meal due to unemployment, lavished the highest praise on this dish. He polished off 28 glazed donut rings and 8 pots of mung bean sukiyaki, and somehow kept it all down. No one has ever managed that before.

...

This recommendation is made solely for promotional purposes on behalf of the Upside-Down Restaurant. For reservations, please call: 100-AEX-118
